strategy.bottleneck: [compute/mainloop-bound] The CUTLASS TF32 implicit-GEMM conv (both conv3x3 calls) is 82.9% of steady per-forward GPU time (18,433us/24 launches = 768us each; 1,536us of the 1,854us forward). Mid shape does 77.3 GFLOP per conv (M=65536,N=256,K=2304), i.e. ~100 TFLOPS on a single fixed 128x128x16 / 64x64x16 / 3-stage tile — one geometry, never tuned, only 4 warps/CTA and 8 warps/SM.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Mainloop tile/pipeline retune of the owned CUTLASS conv: instantiate several DefaultConv2dFprop configs (larger CTA tiles 256x128x16 and 128x256x16, deeper 4-stage 128x128x16, alternate warp partition 32x64x16 for 8 warps/CTA) and pick per problem shape via a one-time cached autotune, falling back to today's config. Directly attacks the 82.9% kernel: more warps/scheduler to hide smem->register latency and fewer CTAs re-filling activation tiles, at identical TF32 precision.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Refactor `conv3x3_nhwc_into` into a template `template<class TB, class Warp, int Stages, int Swizzle> void conv_run(x,w,out,stream)` that instantiates exactly today's DefaultConv2dFprop (float NHWC A/B/C, OpClassTensorOp, Sm80, MMA 16x8x8, LinearCombination<float,4>, kOptimized, alpha=1,beta=0) with TB/Warp/Stages/Swizzle as parameters. No epilogue, iterator or precision change: everything stays fp32 storage + TF32 MMA + fp32 accumulate.
2. Instantiate a fixed candidate list (compile-time), each with its shared-memory budget checked against the 99KB/block limit before use:
   - C0 = 128x128x16, warp 64x64x16, stages 3  -> smem (128+128)*16*4*3 = 49KB  (current; permanent fallback)
   - C1 = 256x128x16, warp 64x64x16, stages 3  -> (256+128)*16*4*3 = 73.7KB, 8 warps/CTA
   - C2 = 128x256x16, warp 64x64x16, stages 3  -> 73.7KB, 8 warps/CTA
   - C3 = 128x128x16, warp 32x64x16, stages 4  -> (128+128)*16*4*4 = 65.5KB, 8 warps/CTA
   - C4 = 128x128x32, warp 64x64x32, stages 3  -> 98.3KB (skip if > device sharedMemPerBlockOptin)
   Query cudaDeviceGetAttribute(cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin) once; drop any candidate above it. CUTLASS's initialize() already does the cudaFuncSetAttribute opt-in for >48KB.
3. Guard each candidate with `op.can_implement(args) == kSuccess`; any failure or non-success launch status removes it from the pool (never let a bad config reach the output).
4. Shape dispatch / anti-regression: compute ctas = ceil(M/TB::kM) * ceil(256/TB::kN) with M = N*H*W. Reject candidates whose ctas < 170 (one partial wave) unless C0 is also below 170; this protects the small (M=8192) and awkward (M=17161) shapes where a 256-row tile would leave <64 CTAs.
5. One-time autotune, cached: static std::map keyed by (N,H,W,C,K). On first call for a key, run each surviving candidate on the real tensors (writing to the real output buffer, idempotent since beta=0) with cudaEvent timing, 1 warmup + 3 timed reps, and store the winner index; all later calls launch only the winner. Total cost is a few hundred us on the first forward only, amortised over the benchmark loop. If timing or any launch errors, store C0.
6. Also sweep Swizzle in {1,4,8} for the winning tile only (second, cheap pass) — helps L2 locality of the K=C*R*S=2304 reduction with only 1-2 N-tiles.
7. Keep every other kernel byte-identical (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial/finalize, gn_silu, gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw, kcrs2krsc), keep buffer reuse (z1=xh, y2=y1) and the deterministic per-chunk partials, so numerical results and the odd-HW tail behaviour are unchanged.
8. Validate on all four shapes (8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) before accepting; if the autotuned winner is not faster than C0 for a key, the cache stores C0 so the round cannot regress.
strategy.evidence: Nsight Systems: CUTLASS implicit GEMM = 82.9% steady time, 18,433us over 24 launches (768us/conv); the per-forward sum 22,245us/12 = 1,854us matches the measured 1.848ms mid-shape wall time, so 1,536us/forward is conv. Root cause: a single untuned 128x128x16 tile with 64x64 warps = only 4 warps/CTA (~8 warps/SM at 49KB smem), too few warps/scheduler to hide the fp32 smem->register + TF32 convert latency; the tile geometry was never varied. Refutation of the 'memory kernels are the bottleneck' alternative: gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw (8.1%) is at 88.7% DRAM SOL, nchw2nhwc (4.6%) at 86.6%, gn_partial at 81.5% — all bandwidth-capped, so even zeroing every non-conv kernel caps the round at 17.1% (Amdahl).
strategy.expected_metric_change: Conv kernel gpu__time_duration down 10-25% (768us -> 580-690us per launch on the mid shape); sm__throughput / achieved TFLOPS on the conv up; sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active for the conv up (8 warps/CTA configs); DRAM throughput of the untouched GN/transpose kernels unchanged at 81-89%. Anti-regression: candidate pool is filtered by can_implement + smem-limit + CTA-count>=170, and the per-shape cache defaults to the current 128x128x16 config, so no shape (especially 2x64x64 and 1x131x131) can be slower than today; output must stay within max_atol 0.0027-0.003 on all four shapes.
